included: Offline vanilla GALE01 gameplay and presentation, including the source-enumerated fighters, moves, costumes, transformations, partner and boss entities, stages, items, CPU, local multiplayer, VS rules, single-player modes, minigames, events, menus, results, unlocks, trophies, movies, save and memory-card behavior, audio, graphics, input and browser lifecycle
Compiled WebAssembly execution using the pinned original source routines, source identities and disc-derived assets
The current original CSS to SSS to match to CSS path as a partial integration baseline
excluded: Netplay, online services and rollback transport
Custom fighters, custom stages, mods and user-authored content
Non-vanilla product extras and revisions other than the pinned GALE01 revision 2 source
Tournament acceptance or a claim that the browser is already a complete game
limitations: Version 1 decomposes the 26 playable CharacterKind identities and 31 named VS-stage slots. Items, mode-specific entities and service categories still require source-identity decomposition before they can serve as a fine-grained completion list.

Statuses are scoped observations, not percentages. A source path, parser, compile, synthetic scene, short prefix or recorded-queue comparison does not by itself pass browser gameplay, retail equivalence, pixels, PCM, input latency or performance.

The eight-fighter/four-stage starting baseline and every added development candidate have partial claims only; source integration does not imply complete moves, costumes, CPU, four-player local input, audio, results, save progression or mode coverage.

The fine-grained VS-stage census covers named StKind values from St_Kind_Izumi through St_Kind_Last; Dummy/Test and route, minigame and other mode-only stage slots remain represented by the aggregate stage rows until their callers are decomposed.
STATUS.md remains the changing evidence index. This inventory links stable evidence documents and receipts without copying measurements from STATUS.md.
Missing or untested behavior stays represented as not_integrated or not_evaluated until an owner records the required source, browser and reference gates.

features.title: Current four-stage source/runtime boundary
pass_criteria: Final Destination, Battlefield, Yoshi's Story and Dream Land retain their source StKind/GrKind, map descriptors, collision, lights, camera, effects, background schedulers and primary music identities.
Each of the four stage owners repeats source initialization, gameplay services, deferred objects, match exit and teardown without borrowing another stage's data or callback.
Browser ordinary input, cold/warm preparation, audio, pixels, retail comparison and performance remain separate gates for every stage.
features.next_step: Split the four stage rows into stage-specific data, map, callback, collision, article, visual and acceptance features before expanding the stage roster.

features.title: Stage-specific movement, hazards, routes and background services
pass_criteria: Moving platforms, scrolling/route stages, hazards, stage Articles, stage-owned objects, camera changes and background transitions execute with their original process order and parameters.
Collision, lights, shadows, effects, animation paths and stage-owned item tables remain alive for the exact source lifetime and are restored on exit.
A stage-specific trace reaches each authored scheduler transition rather than accepting a static map preview.
features.next_step: Enumerate map and scheduler callbacks from each gr source file and assign a lifecycle trace to each unique service family.

features.title: Common items, item physics, drops, articles and item lifecycle
pass_criteria: Every source ItemKind, common item, character article, Pokémon, monster, projectile, effect article and item-related fighter action has an explicit owner and authored table bound.
Spawn/drop rules, collision, pickup/throw, damage, animation, material, effects, audio, persistence, owner changes and teardown match source traces.
Items can be enabled or disabled through original VS rules without silently skipping required item services.
features.next_step: Generate the item-kind census from it/forward.h and map each row to its source implementation, archive data and consuming fighter/stage modes.

features.title: CPU opponents, levels, decisions and source-generated input
pass_criteria: CPU levels 1 through 9, character-specific decision tables, command generation, targeting, item use, team/partner behavior and source RNG consumption match original references.
Two-, three- and four-player CPU configurations preserve player slots, difficulty, costumes, stage, rules, camera, draw and ending state.
Generated input is compared at its source producer; equal final outcomes or a recorded queue alone do not pass live CPU timing.
features.next_step: Split CPU levels, decision families, player counts and item-aware behavior into bounded reference workloads with first-divergence reports.

features.title: Local two-, three- and four-player routing
pass_criteria: Four local controller slots preserve source PAD sampling, player records, ports, teams, costumes, stocks, names, markers, HUD and teardown.
Simultaneous local input, disconnected/empty slots, controller reassignment, rumble and repeated match entry/exit follow original behavior.
Human local input is validated independently from CPU-generated input and recorded-queue replay.
features.next_step: Add physical and ordinary-input two-, three- and four-human recipes with source PAD boundary and teardown evidence.

features.title: VS rules, options, teams, stocks, time, items and match handoff
pass_criteria: Every original VS rule field and option reaches StartMeleeData with its authored default, bounds, save state, RNG/music effect and player/stage handoff.
Stock, time, score, team, handicap, damage ratio, items, pause, No Contest, sudden death and match-ending behavior match source references.
Unsupported or missing rules fail at selection or preparation rather than entering a partial match with substituted defaults.
features.next_step: Enumerate rule fields from the source structs and menu mode callers, then add a source/retail/browsing receipt per options family.

features.title: Original title, character select, stage select and menu transitions
pass_criteria: Original CSS/SSS assets, cursors, animations, confirmation/cancellation, held-button behavior, unlock visibility and typed StartMeleeData handoff match the source route.
The browser completes CSS to SSS to match to CSS and repeated entry without an HTML substitute or hidden fixture selection.
Menu sounds, HPS/SSM ownership, language/font data and transition timing are compared independently from gameplay state.
features.next_step: Decompose title, main menu, CSS, SSS, rules and name-entry screens into source mode rows and extend retail transition receipts beyond the current bounded route.

features.title: Results screen, standings, rewards and return routing
pass_criteria: Original match-end ownership enters Results with correct winner, standings, stats, bonuses, replay/save decisions, music, animations and input routing.
Results navigation returns to the correct source menu or next match and releases the prior match's fighters, stage, audio and graphics owners.
The complete route is compared against an independent original reference for every supported player count and relevant mode.
features.next_step: Implement and receipt the Results owner and route only after the current match-end boundary remains source-equivalent; draft PR #44 remains a dependency and the tracking issue is #34.

features.title: Unlock conditions, challengers, stage progress and persistent progression
pass_criteria: Character, stage, mode, trophy and challenge unlock conditions use the source bit masks, counters, RNG and completion records without conflating runtime availability with save progression.
New challenger, continue, retry, overwrite and completion paths match original source behavior and persist only after the original save boundary.
A fresh and previously progressed memory-card fixture repeat the same unlock decisions in the original and browser implementations.
features.next_step: Separate character, stage, mode and trophy unlock tables into source-identity rows and add original/browser persistence receipts.

features.title: Trophy collection, gallery, lottery and figure display
pass_criteria: Every source trophy/figure identity, model, animation, description, unlock state, collection count and display camera is represented.
Gallery, lottery, collection sorting, figure placement, save/load and exit paths use original input, audio, graphics and memory ownership.
Collection updates are compared through the original persistent save boundary and survive repeated browser lifecycle operations.
features.next_step: Census the toy/figure tables and gallery modes from the pinned source, then attach save and visual lifecycle receipts per collection family.

features.title: Classic, Adventure, All-Star and single-player progression
pass_criteria: Each source single-player mode has explicit stage/opponent order, rules, continue/lives, difficulty, bonus, boss, camera, music, transition and save ownership.
Mode-specific variants such as giant, invisible, stamina and sudden-death behavior execute the original fighter, item, stage and results paths.

features.next_step: Split Classic, Adventure and All-Star into stage-order, opponent-roster, boss, bonus and ending features before implementing their shared runner.

features.title: Event Matches and event-specific fighters, items and stage rules
pass_criteria: Every source event entry, unlock condition, opponent setup, stage, rule override, item/article, timer, win/loss condition and result path is represented.

All event completion and failure branches update progression at the same source save boundary as the original.

features.title: Training, How-To, Multi-Man, Target Test, Home-Run and Stadium minigames
pass_criteria: Each minigame has an explicit source mode, stage, target/object roster, timer/score rules, camera/HUD, input, audio, result and persistence contract.

features.title: Opening movie, movie end, staff roll and THP playback
pass_criteria: Opening, attract, movie-end and staff-roll mode transitions select the original movie assets, language/text data, timing and input behavior.

features.title: Save data, memory-card I/O, initialization and failure recovery
pass_criteria: New card, load, save, overwrite, continue-without-saving, corrupt/missing card, full card, removal and interrupted I/O paths match original source behavior.
Character, stage, mode, trophy, name, controller and settings fields preserve their source masks, endian layout, checksums and save timing.

features.title: AX audio, SSM/HPS banks, voices, effects, music and PCM output
pass_criteria: AX voice allocation, ADPCM/sample residency, SSM/HPS loops, bank lifetimes, effects, crowd, menu music, character themes and true owner transitions preserve source order and timing.

features.title: HSD/GX scene rendering, materials, camera, viewport and presentation
pass_criteria: Source draw order, HSD objects, GX state, materials, textures, palettes, animation, camera, viewport, depth/blend, effects, HUD and magnifier render with original ownership and numeric semantics.
Every admitted fighter, costume, stage, item, menu, result, trophy and movie route has an independent pixel/output comparison at a declared baseline.

features.title: PAD, gamepad, keyboard, rumble, analog thresholds and controller routing
pass_criteria: Raw PAD sampling, normalization, dead zones, triggers, analog thresholds, button chords, held input, keyboard/gamepad mapping and player-port ownership match source behavior.

features.title: Browser startup, preparation, visibility, unload, errors and repeated lifecycle
pass_criteria: Disc/file import, source preparation, explicit readiness, CSS/SSS/match transitions, visibility/focus loss, browser navigation, unload and restart preserve source ownership and clock order.
Every missing/invalid archive, unsupported service, preparation timeout, device error and teardown failure is reported at its owning boundary and leaves no live source object.

features.next_step: Split browser preparation, live loop, visibility/recovery, unload and restart into bounded scenarios with retained failure receipts.
